messages:
marta: Heads-up — we're seeing a coordinated ECC/Xid error wave across a subset of nodes in us-west-2a this morning. Spike started ~02:10 UTC and affects ~9 GPUs across 4 nodes. Pattern looks similar to last quarter's flaky cards but timestamps line up with a driver/firmware rollout last night.

ryan: I saw the alert. quick grep of node logs shows repeated: `Xid 31` + `GPU ECC corrected` on boot cycles. attaching snippet.

kevin: paste the kernel log and nvidia-smi -q error output? we need to confirm if it's ECC corrected or uncorrectable.

marta: log paste: ```kernel: [ 1024.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, pid=0, gfx=0000000123456789
[ 1024.123460] GPU(3b:00): ECC error corrected: 17 counts on memory channel 2
[ 1025.567000] nvidia: GPU 0000:3b:00: GPU lockup, resetting GPU```

alex: interesting — that's the same slot IDs we saw in the June wave but different serials. vendor lot IDs?

jonas: pulled hardware table: impacted serials: [SN-A1-8812, SN-A1-8813, SN-A1-8817, SN-B2-0921]. All from purchase batch A1-2024Q4.

kevin: are these nodes on the firmware/driver combo we rolled last night? I think we pushed driver 525.85 + firmware blob fw-3.2.1 to the pool at 00:30 UTC.

marta: yes, rollout started 00:15 and hit the Dedicated pool in us-west-2a at ~00:45. Canary nodes were green but load was low then.

ryan: ops-bot note: `alert: gpu-ecc-spike us-west-2a (9 gpus) -> paging oncall` :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: I’m on it. Immediate mitigation: recommend draining the 4 affected nodes to reduce job failures. kubectl drain commands next? Considering capacity hit for customer workloads.

alex: we should cordon + migrate high-priority jobs only. Can we do live migrate for CUDA jobs? Not safe; evict/restart on new nodes.

jonas: evict plan: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` then mark node as maintenance. I'll script rollout to avoid taking more than 2 nodes at once.

kevin: vendor-support-bot, have we opened a ticket with the card vendor for these serials and the fw/dr combo? We need an RMA path if it's hardware.

vendor-support-bot: Ticket created: VEND-30921. Summary: "Intermittent ECC corrected + Xid31 resets after 525.85/fw-3.2.1 rollout".

marta: quick triage notes: 1) ECC corrected counts ramp during mixed-concurrency gen2 inference workloads 2) resets coincide with NVLink negotiation retries 3) Only nodes with BIOS power management on (PM=auto) show higher incidence.

ryan: can we rollback driver to 525.70 (previous stable) in the pool for the affected AZ? That would be the fastest hypothesis test.

kevin: rollback plan: tag kernel module build `driver-525.70-rollback` and create a canary group of 3 nodes in us-west-2a to validate. If green, we can schedule a staged rollback across the pool. But this will require node reboots and job disruption.

alex: capacity impact: we have 18 Dedicated GPUs active in AZ. Draining 4 nodes = ~22% capacity loss if those nodes are 8-gpu machines. We should coordinate with sales/customer success and prioritize customer-critical workflows.

jonas: I've started cordoning node infra-gpu-uw2a-13 and infra-gpu-uw2a-21. Running drain on infra-gpu-uw2a-13 now.

marta: NOTE: don't RMA yet. syslogs show ephemeral ECC corrected increments, not immediate uncorrectable errors. Could be firmware regression. RMA will be slow and costly if we misattribute.

sre-oncall: Agreed. Short-term: cordon/drain affected nodes, rollback driver to 525.70 on next maintenance window for the Dedicated pool in us-west-2a. Long-term: open task to enrich our pre-rollout canary to include mixed-concurrency inference load.

kevin: Action items: 1) jonas - finish draining 1 node at a time and tag nodes `maintenance/firmware-regression` (owner) 2) alex - schedule driver rollback canary (525.70) and validate within 2h 3) marta - collect full dmesg + nvlink logs and upload to VEND-30921 4) ryan - notify CS + sales about potential 20% capacity hit in us-west-2a for next 24h.

jonas: done cordon on -13 and -21. drain in progress on -13. No job evictions failed so far.

alex: rolling the canary now: `ansible-playbook rollback-driver.yml -e driver_version=525.70 -l uw2a-canary` will take ~12 minutes per node for reboot+smoke.

vendor-support-bot: Vendor responded: "We are investigating firmware/driver interaction with NVLink. Please collect `nvlink -s` and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` outputs. We may request extended telemetry."

marta: uploaded outputs to VEND-30921. Also captured `smart` and PDUs for the affected rack — no obvious power anomalies.

ryan: customer comms drafted: "We're mitigating a GPU driver/firmware issue in us-west-2a; some workloads may be rescheduled temporarily. We'll update within 6 hours." Want me to send now?

kevin: yes, send high-level note. No need to mention serials or RMA. Include ETA for next update.

sre-oncall: Canary nodes back after rollback to 525.70: 0 Xid events in 3h of mixed-concurrency synthetic load. Looks promising.

marta: excellent. Let's pause further rollouts of 525.85 in other AZs until vendor confirms. Keep these 4 nodes in maintenance until vendor follow-up or we RMA.

jonas: marked nodes with `pool:dedicated, maintenance:firmware-regression, fw-rolled-back:tentative` tags.

alex: recommend retrospective: 1) expand canary workload to cover mixed-inference, 2) gate driver rollouts on NVLink stress test, 3) add telemetry for ECC corrected rate to our weekly health dashboard, 4) vendor verification before next firmware bump.

marta: I'll draft a short RCA and postmortem once vendor provides root cause. For now: cause suspected regression in driver/firmware combo interacting with NVLink and BIOS PM settings -> mitigation: rollback driver + cordon affected nodes -> next steps: vendor RMA if hardware confirms.

kevin: timeline: - 02:10 UTC spike observed - 02:30 drain started - 03:10 vendor ticket opened - 04:05 rollback canary started - 07:30 canary validated - 08:00 nodes cordoned, maintenance tag applied.

ryan: thanks all. I'll take care of the customer note and incident record. Please add any missed logs to the ticket. :thumbsup:

vendor-support-bot: Vendor update (later): "Preliminary: driver 525.85 introduced a regression that increases NVLink re-negotiation under PM=auto on certain batches. Recommending rollback. RMA only if uncorrectable ECC observed."

marta: closing temporary mitigations. Keeping postmortem open until vendor confirms final root cause.

sre-oncall: filing internal postmortem ticket PM-8234 and adding action owners. We'll follow up with timeline and cost estimates for any RMAs.

kevin: FYI finance: potential incremental RMA cost estimate if needed ~ $42k-120k depending on replacements. We'll update once vendor confirms.

alex: awesome work — small team response was clean. We'll schedule a debrief tomorrow 09:30 PT.

marta: meeting scheduled. End of thread.
